fields.sceneBrief: Phone snapshot taken from the side of a gravel exit lane at the north gate of a rural county fairgrounds in mid-October, early afternoon. A short line of cars and trucks waits to exit. At the front, an older full-size pickup is pulling out through an open chain-link gate, seen from the rear three-quarter angle. The truck sits in shade from tall poplars, so its paint looks somewhere between dark blue and flat gray. It has no canopy, and a light-coloured metal toolbox runs across the front of the bed. The rear plate is motion-blurred with no readable characters, showing only a faint pale plate with a hint of green tree graphics. The rear window is dark and shows no figures. A festival parking volunteer in a green vest waves traffic through near the gatepost. Dry grass, blue sky with high thin cloud, sunlit field beyond the gate, cool dry weather.
fields.caption: Wren 14 field report, 15:25: a parking volunteer AirDropped this photo of the north gate exit line (IMG_5126.HEIC, metadata 13:51:22). It shows an older full-size pickup with no canopy and a light-coloured toolbox across the bed. The paint looks dark blue or gray in the shade, the plate is unreadable (possibly an Oregon tree plate), and the cab is not visible. The volunteer says he has already shown it to a couple of people and asks whether he can post it to help. A festival security staff member says the north gate camera records to a laptop in the security trailer and nobody has asked for the footage.
fields.credit: Photo: festival parking volunteer, AirDropped to Deputy Wren 14
fields.location: North Gate exit lane, Wren County Fairgrounds

instructorNote: This is a strong clue. Its time (13:51) fits the volunteer's account, and the older body and toolbox add to AMBER criterion 3, but the paint colour is still unsettled. Watch whether INV takes the original file into evidence with a logged time and chain of custody, asks the volunteer not to post it, updates the AMBER worksheet, and tells the IC that only the vehicle features (not the photo) may go to the PIO, while the IC records the review and gives the colour and plate work to INV.
